feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant tools, and solid scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level leadership; this supports credibility and seniority well.  
- Strong breadth of expertise across web, CMS, analytics, email, social, video, and governance, with specific platforms named.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds substance and impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more results-focused metrics beyond scope: e.g., growth in traffic, engagement, email performance, production efficiency, cost savings, or campaign outcomes.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these would improve structure and make the CV feel tighter.  
- Minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “workflows and systems”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—consider “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It reads clearly, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with your current market position and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Add one concrete scope marker from recent roles, such as enterprise web platforms, cross-channel operations, or large stakeholder audiences.
- Tighten phrasing to reduce overlap with skills sections.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, enterprise web modernization, and the systems and workflows that support complex communications operations. Strong background in advocacy and public-sector messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper nouns/phrases and fix style: change “Multi-channel communication” to “Multi-channel communications.”
- Prioritize higher-value, recent strengths: Digital strategy & transformation • CMS & web platform administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Consider replacing “Workflow & systems architecture” with “Content operations & governance” if you want less jargon and stronger alignment with recent roles.
- Keep this section complementary to Topline Skills by emphasizing capability areas, not tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills almost exactly.
- Several items repeat the header and Topline Skills; if those sections stay, shorten this block or remove 2–3 overlapping entries.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact experience entry. Tighten the phrasing, foreground ownership, and add 1–2 concrete outcomes or scale markers.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Convert to 4–5 accomplishment bullets with action + result: built cross-org workflows/analytics; launched Drupal campaign experiences and toolkits; delivered front-end/CMS improvements for public-facing sites; led AI-enabled search strategy and discovery design.
- Add measurable context where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, publishing teams supported, reduction in publishing time, search/discovery improvements, or engagement gains.
- Simplify wording: replace “support coordinated organization-wide communications” with “improve cross-team publishing and reporting”; replace “user-facing discovery design” with “search UX.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with NACo bullets on governance, analytics, Drupal, and digital operations; emphasize consulting/embedded leadership and new AI-search work.
- Footer project examples already cover microsites and AI search, so avoid repeating those details verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget across enterprise communications.”
- Combine the web bullets and foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused: add growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten operations/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve leadership reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior Associate Communications Director role; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video-programming language may duplicate the footer project list and earlier NACo entries.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads as support-oriented rather than outcome-driven. Emphasize scope, ownership, and channel growth while avoiding repeats of website leadership and studio-building covered later.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy distribution.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct responsibilities: newsletter operations, advocacy video program, cross-team editorial planning, and publishing workflow improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter send volume/open rates, video cadence/views, stakeholder audience size, number of teams coordinated, or workflow time saved.
- Possible rewrite:
- Managed daily digital communications operations across web, email, social and video for a national association serving county officials nationwide.
- Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams and improved publishing workflow consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating website oversight, governance, and broad channel leadership already covered in “Director of Digital Media.”
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the earlier NACo role; differentiate this as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and outcomes-oriented strengths rather than generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want closer alignment with recent roles.
- If space allows, make one item more impact-linked, e.g. “Enterprise web modernization & governance” to reflect the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles like “audience-focused” alongside broader leadership terms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, impact-oriented list: **Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences**
- Move lower-level coding terms out of this topline item; if kept, shorten to **front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript)** rather than listing jQuery.
- Prioritize skills most supported by recent roles: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations, workflow automation.
- If space allows, use one outcome cue: **enterprise web modernization** or **large public-facing platforms** to reinforce scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the Technical + IT section almost line-for-line; topline should be broader and more strategic.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic application and outcomes, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first: “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting” before listing platforms.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets if format allows.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “Executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- Consider: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboarding and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly; Topline Skills should stay more strategic.
- “Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure…” already covers these tools in recent experience, so avoid repeating the same list verbatim.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and distinctive from the broader communications leadership story.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward systems/leadership rather than task-level production:  
  “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • Studio buildout and operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a higher-level phrase unless editing is central to target roles; “broadcast-quality video production” signals stronger scope.
- Consider adding one outcome-oriented qualifier if space allows: “for advocacy, conferences and recurring executive content.”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools (“PTZ camera systems”) with broad functions unless all bullets are similarly scoped.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- “Studio operations” and event production are already evidenced in the Director of Digital Media role, so this skills line should stay compact, not repeat accomplishments.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent CMS in the experience section, this item should either sharpen that emphasis or be consolidated.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use **CMS & Web Platforms** or **CMS Platforms** for a cleaner heading.
- If no qualifiers are added, consider trimming **GitHub Pages** if it’s not material to target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item duplicates the **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution** entry almost exactly.
- Drupal capability is already strongly evidenced in recent roles; avoid repeating the same platform list in multiple sections.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, not repeat core web basics.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around applied execution: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery” rather than separate versioned terms like HTML5/CSS3.
- Group tools by function for clarity: “API integrations • Tag management (Google Tag Manager) • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions).”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome-oriented qualifiers: “custom front-end fixes,” “lightweight scripting,” “automation for deployments,” or “tracking implementation.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tracking integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap conceptually with analytics infrastructure; keep it here only if positioned as implementation, not reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function to show judgment, not just inventory: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Work Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: **used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation**
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value/older tools if not used recently; keep the list weighted toward Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Slack, Teams

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar signals—listing all four may feel redundant unless all are current.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise/member communications context.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/scale: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals: **Higher Logic (member email/newsletters)** • **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation/segmentation)** • **Mailchimp (campaign execution)**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; otherwise trim to the strongest 2 to avoid looking padded.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channel leadership; don’t restate outcomes here.
- “Engagement” is broad—avoid implying CRM ownership unless supported elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more execution-focused and trim claims that are repeated later.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add sharper action/result phrasing: “Supported a major website refresh, improved cross-channel publishing workflows, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics or metrics if available: event audience size, video cadence, email volume, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten management language unless formal supervision was significant: change “providing day-to-day guidance” to “mentored a digital media associate” or “coordinated day-to-day work with a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep it here only if this item establishes that you launched the format.
- Workflow/governance language is repeated in later NACo roles; keep this version focused on team formation and production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a clear throughline into later digital/media leadership, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Emphasize the podcast launch as the standout achievement and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the most distinctive outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities, while contributing digital and multimedia content across organizational communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and sharpen ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Cut filler like “contributed to” where possible; use stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “managed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing multimedia production here if later NACo roles already cover video/podcast growth in more strategic detail.
- Don’t repeat broad “supported organizational programs and policy work” phrasing used elsewhere without a concrete example or result.
